newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Ecuador says state phone sell-off price could rise.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says state phone sell-off price could rise.

text.p: The Ecuadorean government said Wednesday the reference sale price for the 35 percent of state telephone company Emetel up for privatization may rise due to high levels of foreign interest.

The head of the government privatization body Conam, Raul Gangotena, told reporters that an international road show "had good results, they all showed their interest in taking part in this process and that is pushing up the price."
The government says it will only reveal the reference price for the 35 percent stake the day before the tender. But previous estimates have valued it at $1.2 billion.

Ecuador plans to privatize Emetel in September, after its division into two operating units to avoid the local phone market becoming a private monopoly. The sale was originally planned for April, but was delayed by the ouster of President Abdala Bucaram in early February.
MCI and GTE of the United States, Italy's Stet, Telefonica de Espana and Korea Telecom all signed up for the Emetel partial privatization process last November.
The prospectus costing $30,000 will be put on sale next Monday.
